rules.title: FEHA ban on source-of-income discrimination (including Section 8 vouchers)
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent to, or apply different terms to, applicants or tenants based on how they will pay rent, including Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers and other rental assistance. They must also comply with rental assistance program requirements such as paperwork and inspections, and may not advertise 'No Section 8.'
rules.coverage_conditions: Most housing accommodations and housing providers in California, including landlords, property managers and tenant screening companies.
rules.exemptions: An owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics, but may not publish discriminatory statements or advertisements.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemption for an owner-occupant renting to one additional person

rules.penalty: Remedies include out-of-pocket losses, injunction, access to the denied housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”). This includes the State of California’s COVID-19 Rent Relief Program, Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers, (SSI) social security disability benefits, or wages earned from a job.

rules.title: FEHA limits on criminal history screening
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not impose blanket bans on people with criminal histories. They may not consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and a denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and the time elapsed.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most housing providers in California, including landlords and tenant screening companies.
rules.exemptions: An owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person is exempt.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemption for an owner-occupant renting to one additional person

rules.penalty: Remedies include out-of-pocket losses, injunction, access to the denied housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
